 38s ago 08.39 EDT 50 min A promising City attack ends when Anderson overhits a cross from the De Bruyne Zone. He normally measures his crosses expertly from that position. On this occasion, the ball flies out of play and the home fans whistle with disdain.
 Share Updated at  08.40 EDT 2m ago 08.38 EDT 48 min That header, by the way, was only Haaland’s ninth touch of the game. It’s the tenth, eleventh and twelfth that Villa will be worried about.
 Share 4m ago 08.36 EDT 47 min Villa break after an errant pass from Lewis. Eventually Maatsen pings a shot that ricochets behind for a corner. Cash takes, Haaland wins it in the air and City eventually clear.
 Share 4m ago 08.35 EDT 46 min Back under way. Khusanov has moved infield to centre-back.
 Share 5m ago 08.34 EDT Half-time substitutions
 Manchester City have brought on Phil Foden and Rico Lewis for Marc Guehi and Rayan Cherki.
 Share 17m ago 08.22 EDT Half-time reading 
 I’m looking forward to Older and Calmer, a duet between Jose and Indigo De Souza .
 Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico Read more Share 18m ago 08.21 EDT Half time: Aston Villa 1-0 Man City
 A raw, compelling first half at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson’s early goal capped a ferocious start from Villa – who had more than 90% of the possession at that stage – and set up a fascinating clash of styles.
 City dominated the ball for the rest of the half: the impressive Iliman Ndiaye hit the post and was one of two City players to have penalty appeals turned down. But Villa, with Jackson and John McGinn outstanding, were a constant menace in transition.
 In short: cracking game, more please!
 Share 21m ago 08.18 EDT 45 min One minute of added time. Cherki’s curving pass towards Haaland is cut out by the last defender Lindelof. There was a lot of grass behind Lindelof but Cherki didn’t quite get the pass right.
 Share 23m ago 08.17 EDT 44 min Ndiaye’s deflected cross is claimed at the second attempt by Suzuki. City’s wide players have been a big threat.
 Share 25m ago 08.14 EDT 42 min Pound for pound, Unai Emery is the best manager in the world: discuss.
 (I don’t know whether I think this, but it’s surely up for discussion. It’s astonishing that he has them playing this well so soon after losing Martinez, Konsa, Digne, Rogers, Tielemans, Rogers, Watkins.)
 Share 27m ago 08.12 EDT 40 min: Great tackle by Dias!
 Alysson moves elegantly into the area from the right, hugging the ball on his left foot. He zig-zags between Dias and another City player and is about to shoot – probably score – when Dias makes a fabulous recovery tackle.
 Share 29m ago 08.11 EDT 38 min Cherki loses the ball to Manzanbi, pulls him back to stop a Villa break and is booked. Villa have kept Cherki very quiet in his day job.
 Share 31m ago 08.09 EDT 37 min There’s a cracking atmosphere at Villa Park: constant hostility from the home fans, period defiance from the away end.
 Another good run from Doku leads to a City corner. Enzo Fernandez takes, Kamara heads away at the near post.
 Share 33m ago 08.06 EDT 34 min … and Manzanbi whacks it over the bar. A poor effort by his standards.
 Share 34m ago 08.06 EDT 33 min The free-kick is just outside the area, slightly to the left of centre…
 Share Updated at  08.06 EDT 34m ago 08.05 EDT 32 min Guehi is booked for fouling Jackson just outside the area. It was a bit of a wrestling match, and Guehi didn’t think he’d committed the foul. The home fans, by contrast, thought it should have been a Dogso red card. I’m pretty sure there was a covering defender.
 With Villa seeing very little of the ball in the last 25 minutes, Nicolas Jackson has been fantastic .
 Share 35m ago 08.04 EDT 31 min Now City want a penalty when Maatsen, who is really struggling, misses a lunging tackle at Ndiaye, who then goes over. Hard to tell whether he was fouled or whether he slipped. It was clumsy from Maatsen but it’s been cleared by VAR.
 View image in fullscreen Iliman Ndiaye is up-ended by Ian Maatsen. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  08.08 EDT 37m ago 08.03 EDT 31 min “I’ve come late to the MBM and need to warn you not to put ideas into people’s heads,” writes Richard Hirst. “At the rate Man City are collecting points a 50 point deduction would be nowhere near enough to ensure that they finish below Fulham.”
 Share 37m ago 08.02 EDT 30 min Manzanbi goes over in the area after running into Anderson. The Villa fans want a penalty but the referee isn’t interested; nor are VAR. It looked like Anderson just stood his ground.
 Share 38m ago 08.02 EDT 29 min “Fantastic reading in the lee of Mt Ventoux that Villa have taken the lead,” writes Mike Daniels. “Nowhere to watch but thanks for the live report.”
 You are most welcome.
 Share 39m ago 08.01 EDT 28 min: Ndiaye hits the post!
 Ndiaye been so sharp on the right. He cuts inside again, away from Maatsen, and sweps a left-foot curler across goal from the edge of the area. It beats the diving Suzuki, bounces up and hits the outside of the far post.
 Share 40m ago 07.59 EDT 26 min A quick free-kick from McGinn, whose football brain is as big as his backside, leads to a corner that is punched away by Donnarumma. Terrific game, this - the clash of styles, the tempo, the slight edge that is going to lead to a shoving match any minute now.
 Share 42m ago 07.58 EDT 24 min Another good run from Doku forces Villa into some desperate defending. They are simultaneously hanging on at 1-0, and threateningt to make it 2-0 whenever they break.
 Share 45m ago 07.54 EDT 21 min Doku crackles past Alysson on the edge of the area and fires a low cross at Cherki. He sweeps a first-time shot towards goal and Suzuki falls on the ball to his left. Comfortable save.
 Suzuki then belts the ball downfield and out for a throw-in in the City half. “If in doubt, ping one out,” says the TNT Sports commentator Darren Fletcher.
 Share 48m ago 07.52 EDT 19 min Enzo Fernandez appeals for a penalty after a slight shove from Joao Gomes. Villa break, with Jackson all alone. He runs at a backpedalling defence before dragging a shot wide from the edge of the area.
 VAR don’t intervene on the Fernandez incident. Gomes took a risk – both hands on the back – but I guess it falls under referee’s call.
 Share Updated at  07.53 EDT 49m ago 07.51 EDT 17 min Loads of City pressure now, though Villa are a constant threat on the break.
 Share 53m ago 07.46 EDT 13 min: Fine save by Suzuki! This is a cracking match. Ndiaye cuts inside from the right, beats two defenders and curls a fast left-foot shot towards the corner from 20 yards. Suzuki dives a long way to his right to push it away with both hands.
 Share 1h ago 07.41 EDT 9 min That’s woken City up. Gvardiol breaks into the area and reverse a cross that is deflected behind by Lindelof.
 Share 1h ago 07.40 EDT Dias’s risky crossfield pass was miscontrolled on the right by Guehi, allowing McGinn to push the ball into the penalty area for Jackson. He shuffled back inside Anderson, whose attempted tackle was a bit lazy, and lifted an emphatic sidefoot finish past Donnarumma. That was so cool from Jackson, who already has six goals for Villa.
 Share Updated at  07.43 EDT 1h ago 07.39 EDT GOAL! Aston Villa 1-0 Man City (Jackson 6)
 Nicolas Jackson caps a blistering start from Aston Villa!
 View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson rifles Villa into an early lead! Photograph: Morgan Harlow/AP View image in fullscreen Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters Share Updated at  07.43 EDT 1h ago 07.38 EDT 6 min … which almost leads to a goal. McGinn took it short on the left, got it back and picked out the onrushing Alysson on the edge of the area. His fierce first-time shot was crucially blocked by Guehi.
 Villa have had 92% possession. Yep.
 Share 1h ago 07.37 EDT 5 min Donnarumma is penalised for taking too long over the goalkick, so Villa have a bonus corner…
 Share 1h ago 07.37 EDT 4 min Villa work the ball nicely across the face of the City area before Cash’s cross is turned behind by Guehi. McGinn drives a long corner to Maatsen, whose sidefoot volley flies over the bar.
 Share 1h ago 07.34 EDT 2 min Guehi makes a good sliding tackle on Manzambi just outside the area. Villa have started well.
 Share 1h ago 07.33 EDT 1 min The players take a knee before Villa kick off from right to left as we watch.
 Share 1h ago 07.32 EDT There’s another big lunchtime game in the WSL. You can join Billy Munday for that.
 Tottenham host Arsenal in WSL, Premier League, EFL and more – football clockwatch live Read more Share 1h ago 07.29 EDT Saying which, there’s a sudden chorus of boos – I’m not exactly sure why because the TV coverage is showing the Villa line-up.
 Share 1h ago 07.29 EDT The players walk out of the tunnel, into the Birmingham rain. It doesn’t sound espeically hostile, although you can’t always tell on TV. The City fans are once again tooled up with inflatable bananas.
 Share 1h ago 07.25 EDT “Hi Rob,” writes Gary Naylor. “Barreling down the péage from Girona to Avignon, having spent the morning in the Dali Museum (still a third rater if you ask me), I have a moral dilemma. Can we ask Grok to direct us to a bar showing the Everton match? Or would that be shaking hands with both the AI and Musk devils? It was easier when you just had to wait until Monday afternoon and pick up a Guardian International for 50 francs.”
 Heh. I remember reading Austria Vienna 5-1 Manchester United in the results section in August 1991. That was – and still is – the extent of my knowledge about the game. The papers didn’t cover the game, because it was still the cricket season.
 Share Updated at  07.28 EDT 1h ago 07.10 EDT Enzo Maresca on the omission of Phil Foden 
 double quotation mark The good thing is that because we play so many games we have so many players available and to choose from. We want to keep the players fresh and fit.
 Next!
 Joking and next!ing aside, it’s a sign of the times that Foden scored a hat-trick on Wednesday yet most people expected him to be left out today.
 Share Updated at  07.15 EDT 2h ago 06.57 EDT Elliot Anderson has been chatting to TNT Sports . When asked whether he expected City to receive another hostile reception – this is their first away game since Anfield – he chuckled and said: “Yeah, probably. Everywhere we go, we’ll get it.”
 Share 2h ago 06.53 EDT On this day in 2022… Unai Emery was appointed as Villa’s head coach. The jury were released a long time ago.
 Aston Villa confirm Unai Emery as manager after paying €6m clause Read more Share 2h ago 06.49 EDT Unai Emery’s pre-match thoughts 
 double quotation mark It’s a huge, huge challenge today. They are a team who try to dominate, to impose their positioning, their skills and their tactical structure. We must be so intense in our focus and in our actions. Then, when we have the ball, we have try to threaten them. It’s a huge challenge, collectively and individually, against the best team in the league right now.
 View image in fullscreen Unai Emery ready for ‘huge challenge today’. Photograph: David Davies/PA Share Updated at  07.15 EDT 2h ago 06.38 EDT City have been beaten on their last three visits to Villa Park: 1-0 December 2023, 2-1 in December 2024 and 1-0 last October.
 Villa also won at the Etihad in May, which sealed their first league double over City since 1962-63. What does it all mean?
 Share Updated at  06.45 EDT 2h ago 06.31 EDT “There are no coincidences in life,” writes Krishnamoorthy V. “Your mention of The Shining in the preamble connects to The Overlook Hotel. Is it a reference to what the Premier League will do in its assessment of City’s appeal?”
 You are the caretaker.
 Share 2h ago 06.30 EDT Team news: Foden back on the bench
 Unai Emery and Enzo Maresca continue their policy of rotation, rotation, rotation. Matty Cash, Ian Maatsen, Boubacar Kamara and Johan Manzambi return to the Villa team in place of Tyrone Mings, Ibrahim Mbaye, Ross Barkley and Emi Buendia.
 Phil Foden, who scored a hat-trick against AEK in the week, is back on the City bench. Marc Guehi, Iliman Ndiaye, Jeremy Doku and Erling Haaland come into the team; the other players to drop out are Rico Lewis, Allan and Floyd Samba.
 Aston Villa (4-2-3-1) Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Joao Gomes; Alysson, Manzambi, McGinn; Jackson.
 Subs: Bizot, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Mbaye, Bogarde, Goretzka, Madjo, Hemmings.
 Man City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.
 Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait Nouri, Vitor Reis, Bouaddi, O’Reilly, Foden, McAidoo, Lewis.
 Referee Peter Bankes (Merseyside)
 View image in fullscreen Someone’s looking forward to seeing John McGinn. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock Share Updated at  07.26 EDT 2h ago 06.14 EDT Bayern Munich say their head coach Vincent Kompany , who was taken to hospital after collapsing during training on Friday, will be absent for “weeks rather than days”. Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital.
 You can read about that, and all the rest of the day’s fitba news, on our matchday live blog.
 Mourinho labels Madrid-Barça comparison ‘unfair’, Kompany to miss ‘weeks’ say Bayern, and more Read more Share 2h ago 06.11 EDT It was five months ago but it feels a lot longer. When these two sides met in May to finish the season, the contest doubled as Pep Guardiola’s leaving party after 10 years in the job and twice as many trophies, an era now laden with asterisks. It must be surreal for Aston Villa supporters, too. Their 2-1 victory at the Etihad Stadium, inspired by two goals from Ollie Watkins to complete a league double over City, came only four days after their Europa League triumph in Istanbul, where Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Emi Buendía were the scorers.
 Buendía is the only one left in claret and blue as Unai Emery builds a new side, one that has picked up in form after a single point from their first four league games. City, meanwhile, are thriving on the pitch: victory would make them just the third side to win their first eight games of a Premier League season.
 Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend Read more Share 3h ago 06.00 EDT Preamble
 You remember Manchester City , don’t you? They made one or two headlines earlier in the month, but have since been kept off the back pages by a neighbouring circus.
 Since the weird (and wonderful, if you’re a City fan) win at Anfield, Enzo Maresca’s team have played three games, all at home. They were undressed by PSG, held off Ipswich last weekend and hammered AEK on Tuesday. Oh, and Elliot Anderson made the James Bond shortlist .
 City are top of the Premier League with a perfect record of seven wins from seven. But like life, The Shining and those dreams in which all your teeth fall out, nobody really knows what it means. City are on 21 points, but for all we know it could effectively be -29. Yes, I have just pulled that number from my fundament. No, I don’t have any inside knowledge.
 The only thing the City players – who, lest we forget, had nowt to do with the 115 charges – can win football matches and see where it takes them.
 Today’s will be tougher than most. Unai Emery has somehow squashed a year of transition into a month. Villa lost six of their Europa League-winning XI in the summer and started the season terribly. But they have won five of the last six games and are playing with a rhythm that belies the summer rebuild. On recent evidence, losing all those great players really was just a flesh wound.
 Kick off 12.30pm.
